title: Replace a helmet visor
instruction: Release both catches and replace the raised visor with the spare. Close and reopen the replacement to check both sides are secure, then put the old visor in the tray and let go.
context: A curved visor must be aligned at two spaced hinge bases and retained by both catches. A successful fit must still open and close.
setup: An inert full-size helmet shell (290 × 236 × 250 mm) is secured to a 220 mm display base on a 747.5 mm-high table. Its centre is at (220, 0, 135) mm above the table. The 2 mm curved polycarbonate visor is raised 70°, retained at hinge bases 264 mm apart; each base has a 10 × 14 mm downward spring-release button with 4 mm travel. A matching spare rests at (170, −300) mm. A 310 × 280 mm tray is centred at (180, 300) mm. The fixed layout and generic catch geometry are supplied in geometry.py. Both arms use 40 × 10 × 1 mm replacement precision fingers with silicone contact faces and 6 N jaw effort.
scoring: Broken parts score zero. Otherwise award the highest applicable score: 0.25 when the old visor is released from both catches; 0.5 when one replacement catch is engaged; 0.75 when both are engaged. Full score also requires closing the replacement to within 8° of shut, reopening it by at least 55°, placing the old visor on the tray, and releasing both hands for two seconds with both catches still engaged. Other outcomes score zero. Judge catch retention and movement from the video; a simple angle template and ruler suffice.
fidelity: The visor has a rigid curved centre and compliant end ears. Spring trigger movement releases the native hinge constraints. Local hook seating is approximated by capture within 2.5 mm and 6 degrees at low speed; no object pose is written. This is a generic two-catch quick-release design, not a certified replacement part. The helmet is inert and not worn by a person.
scores: Development only: not validated; do not submit.
reset_notes: Replace any damaged visor, ears or catch components. Remove the replacement, refit the original with both catches engaged at 70°, and return the spare to its pictured position. This uses an inert display assembly, never protective equipment worn by a person. The generic hinge geometry is a task proxy, not a certified commercial replacement.
